problem: At the school book fair, Mr. Takeda paid $63 for 9 copies of the same comic. Each copy cost the same amount. How much was one copy?
follow_up_questions: A colleague wants 4 copies of that comic. How much will the colleague pay?
The colleague pays with a $50 note. What change does the colleague get?
How much did Mr. Takeda and his colleague spend on comics in total?

problem: What is the price of one bag of birdseed if Lucia spent $63 at the garden centre on 9 bags that all cost the same?
follow_up_questions: Her friend Bram buys 4 of those bags. What does Bram pay?
Bram pays with a $50 note. How much should he get back?
Altogether, how much did Lucia and Bram spend on birdseed?

problem: A tailor paid $9 for a 48-inch strip of lace. She cuts it into 6 equal pieces, one for each dress she is sewing. How long is each piece?
follow_up_questions: Each dress also needs a button, and buttons cost $2 each. What do the buttons for all the dresses cost?
She pays for the buttons with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?

problem: How long will each streamer be? Ayesha spent $9 on a 48-metre roll of crepe paper, and she is cutting it into 6 equal streamers, one for every classroom door.
follow_up_questions: Every door also needs a roll of tape, and tape is $2 a roll. What does the tape for all the doors cost?
She hands over a $20 bill for the tape. What change does she receive?

problem: The village bakery has 45 apples. Every apple pie needs 5 apples. The baker wears a striped apron. How many pies can she bake?
follow_up_questions: Each pie is cut into 8 slices. How many slices will there be altogether?

problem: How many birdhouses can Grandpa Teodor build? His workshop smells of fresh pine. He has 45 nails, and every birdhouse takes 5 of them.
follow_up_questions: Each birdhouse needs 8 wooden shingles for its roof. How many shingles will he need in all?

problem: Down at the lake, the boat hire hut asks $4 for each hour a canoe is out. Svetlana keeps a canoe for 9 hours. Find what she owes.
What will Kenji pay for parking? He leaves his van in the stadium car park for 9 hours, and parking there costs $4 per hour.
At the ice cream parlour, a sundae is one flavour of ice cream with one topping. There are 6 flavours and 4 toppings. How many different sundaes can be made?
follow_up_questions: The parlour adds 2 new toppings. How many different sundaes are possible now?
Benedikt wants to taste every sundae, one on each visit. He has already had 9 of them. How many are still left for him to try?

problem: Pick one hat and one scarf: how many different outfits can the doll in the toy shop window wear, if there are 6 hats and 4 scarves to choose from?
follow_up_questions: The shop owner knits 2 more scarves. How many different outfits are there now?
Amira is taking a photo of every outfit. She has photographed 9 so far. How many outfits are left to photograph?

problem: A librarian can repair 8 torn books in an hour. There are 40 books in the repair pile. How many hours will she need to fix them all?
follow_up_questions: She is paid $9 for each hour of work. How much does she earn for the job?

problem: How many hours will it take Mr. Osei to mark 40 science tests, if he marks 8 tests every hour?
follow_up_questions: For marking, he gets $9 per hour. What does he earn for all of it?

problem: In the school garden, the children planted tulip bulbs in 7 rows, with 9 bulbs in each row. Find how many bulbs they planted.
follow_up_questions: Every bulb cost $2. What did all the bulbs cost?
The parents' club paid $50 of that, and the school paid the rest. How much did the school pay?
The school paid its share in 4 equal amounts. How much was each amount?

problem: How many chairs are in the hall? For the talent show, the caretaker set out 7 rows of chairs, and every row has 9 chairs.
follow_up_questions: Renting each chair cost $2. What was the rent for all the chairs?
Ticket sales covered $50 of the rent, and the school budget covered the rest. How much came from the budget?
The budget money was paid out in 4 equal parts. How much was each part?

problem: Selling cookies after school, Marguerite earned $64 this week. Her classmate Tobias earned $16. How many times as much as Tobias did Marguerite earn?
follow_up_questions: Marguerite saves $24 of her money. How much is left for her to spend?
Tobias puts all his money together with Marguerite's spending money to buy a board game. How much do they have for the game?

problem: How many times greater was Dmitri's total than Ines's? At the craft fair, Dmitri's candle table made $64, while Ines's bead table nearby made $16.
follow_up_questions: Dmitri sets aside $24 for new wax. How much does he have left to spend?
Ines adds all her money to Dmitri's spending money to rent a bigger table. How much money do they have for the table?

problem: In the class recycling drive, Chidi collected 72 cans. That was 4 times as many cans as Freya collected. How many cans did Freya collect?
What was the length of the short ribbon? Mrs. Nakamura's long ribbon measured 72 centimetres, and it was 4 times as long as the short one.
The bike rack outside the library has room for 30 bikes. Right now 18 bikes are parked there. The rack was painted green last spring. How many more bikes can fit?
follow_up_questions: A bike tag costs $3. What would it cost to buy tags for that many bikes?

problem: How many more stamps does Kalani need to fill her album page? Her uncle sends her letters from abroad. The page holds 30 stamps, and so far she has stuck 18 on it.
follow_up_questions: Stamps cost $3 each at the hobby shop. What would that many stamps cost her?

problem: Zainab had $37 in her piggy bank. She walked her neighbour's dog for a month and earned $25. How much money does she have now?
follow_up_questions: She buys a book for $18. How much money is left?
Her grandfather doubles what she has left. How much does Zainab have now?

problem: How much is in Benji's wallet now? He started with $37, and then the hardware store paid him $25 for stacking shelves on Saturday.
follow_up_questions: Then he buys an $18 bike helmet. How much money is left?
His mother doubles whatever he has left. How much money does Benji have now?

problem: The juice bar sells 9 kinds of smoothie, and each morning the owner blends 6 litres of every kind. How many litres of smoothie does he blend each morning?
follow_up_questions: By evening, 47 litres have been sold. How much smoothie is left?

problem: Every day a camp kitchen boils 6 litres of each of its 9 kinds of tea. What is the total number of litres it boils daily?
follow_up_questions: The campers drink 47 litres before bedtime. How many litres are left over?

problem: Leandro baked 42 cookies and split them evenly into 6 gift bags for the school fair. How many cookies went into each bag?
follow_up_questions: He sells each bag for $4. How much money does he get for all the bags?
The ingredients had cost him $9. How much did he make once that is taken away?
He makes that same amount at 3 fairs in a row. How much does he earn over those fairs?

problem: How many marbles end up in each pouch? Freya has 42 marbles, and she shares them out evenly into 6 cloth pouches to sell at the craft market.
follow_up_questions: Each pouch sells for $4. What does she get for all of the pouches?
Her table at the market cost $9. How much does she have after paying for it?
She earns that same amount at 3 markets. What does she earn in total?

problem: Kwame bought a $35 football at the sports shop and paid with nothing but $5 bills. How many bills did he give the cashier?
How many five-dollar bills must Ingrid count out for a $35 concert ticket? They are the only kind of bill in her purse.
At the zoo gift shop, a plush penguin costs $13. Aleksander pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get?
follow_up_questions: He spends $4 of his change on a postcard. How much money does he have now?
His aunt gives him $9 for lunch. How much does he have now?

problem: Hira hands over a $20 bill for a $13 paint set at the art shop. What change comes back to her?
follow_up_questions: With some of that change she buys a $4 sketching pencil. How much is left?
Her mother gives her $9 more for the bus. How much money does she have now?

problem: The school library received 8 boxes of new books, with 9 books in each box. By Friday, students had borrowed 29 of them. How many of the new books are still on the shelves?
follow_up_questions: Each book still on the shelves gets a $2 plastic cover. How much do the covers cost in all?

problem: How many pencils are still in the boxes? A stationery shop unpacked 8 boxes holding 9 pencils each, and customers bought 29 pencils before noon.
follow_up_questions: The shop sells each of the remaining pencils for $2. If they all sell, how much money comes in?

problem: Arash picked six apples in the orchard. His cousin Liv picked three times as many. How many apples did Liv pick?
follow_up_questions: Liv gives 7 of her apples to a neighbour. How many does she still have?
How many apples do the two cousins have together now?

problem: On a forest walk, Pita collected six pinecones. How many did his sister Ana collect, if she gathered three times as many?
follow_up_questions: Ana drops 7 of her pinecones in the stream. How many does she have left?
How many pinecones do the brother and sister have together now?

problem: For its summer fair, the football club printed 85 programmes and has already handed out 47. Find how many programmes are left.
How many seed packets are still unsold? A garden club packed 85 of them for the spring sale, and 47 have been bought.
Tomasz takes $50 to the water park. He buys 4 locker tokens that cost $8 each. The wave pool is closed for cleaning. How much money does he have left?
follow_up_questions: He then spends $6 on ice cream. How much is left now?

problem: How much money remains in Adaeze's purse? She brought $50 to the theatre, where seats cost $8 each. The curtains on the stage were deep red. She bought 4 seats for her family.
follow_up_questions: At the interval she buys $6 worth of juice. How much does she have now?

problem: In the school garden, Ines counted 17 red tulips and 26 yellow tulips. How many tulips did she count altogether?
follow_up_questions: Later she found 9 more tulips by the fence. What is her new total?
Her friend Oskar counted 8 fewer tulips than Ines's new total. How many did Oskar count?
How many tulips did Ines and Oskar count together?

problem: How many cars did Kiran count? Sitting by the road, he saw 17 white cars go past, and after that 26 blue ones.
follow_up_questions: Before going inside he saw 9 more cars. What is his total now?
His sister Noor counted 8 fewer cars than Kiran's new total. How many cars did Noor count?
How many cars did Kiran and Noor count in all?

problem: The coach orders balls for the sports club: 34 small ones and 18 big ones. How many balls are in the order altogether?
follow_up_questions: He puts the balls into 4 equal nets. How many balls go in each net?
The small balls cost $2 each. How much did the coach pay for the small balls?

problem: What is the total number of jars Grandma Rosa filled? She made 34 jars of plum jam and 18 jars of peach jam for the village fair.
follow_up_questions: She packs all the jars into 4 boxes with the same number in each. How many jars are in each box?
The plum jam jars sell for $2 each. How much will she get for the plum jam?

problem: Three classmates sold raffle tickets for the library. Aiko sold $25 worth, Bilal sold $30 worth and Carmen sold $40 worth. How much did they sell in total?
How far did the relay team cycle? Over the weekend, Dariusz rode 25 kilometres, Fatou rode 30 kilometres and Gwen rode 40 kilometres.
Ms. Ortega has 48 stickers and shares them equally among the 6 children in her reading group. How many stickers does each child get?
follow_up_questions: One child loses 3 of the stickers on the way home. How many does that child have left?
That child's brother then gives her 4 more stickers. How many stickers does she have now?

problem: How many carrots does each rabbit get when a farmer divides 48 carrots equally among her 6 rabbits?
follow_up_questions: One rabbit buries 3 of its carrots. How many does that rabbit have left to eat?
The farmer's son then gives that rabbit 4 more carrots. How many carrots does it have now?

problem: Beads at the craft shop come in little bags of 8. A busy Saturday saw customers buy 7 bags. What was the number of beads sold?
follow_up_questions: Each bag was $6. How much money did the craft shop take for the beads?

problem: How many tennis balls did the sports store sell on Monday, if it sold 7 tubes and every tube holds 8 balls?
follow_up_questions: Every tube was priced at $6. What did the store earn from the tubes?

problem: On the class trip to the orchard, each of the 9 children picked 4 pears. How many pears did they pick in all?
follow_up_questions: They dropped 15 bruised pears in the compost bin. How many pears did they keep?
The pears they kept were shared equally among 3 classes. How many pears did each class get?
Each class eats 2 of its pears at lunch and saves the rest. How many pears does one class save?

problem: What was the total number of eggs gathered at farm camp, if 9 campers each gathered 4 eggs from the henhouse?
follow_up_questions: Then 15 eggs cracked on the way back. How many whole eggs were left?
The whole eggs were split evenly among 3 cabins. How many eggs did each cabin get?
Each cabin boils 2 of its eggs for breakfast and keeps the others. How many eggs does one cabin keep?

problem: At the school fair, the cake stall raised $34 and the book stall raised $19. How much more did the cake stall raise?
follow_up_questions: The next day, the book stall raised twice what it raised on the first day. How much did it raise on the second day?

problem: By how many points did Arno's team win the quiz? Arno's team scored 34 points, and Bea's team scored 19.
follow_up_questions: In the next quiz, Bea's team scored twice its first score. How many points did it score in the next quiz?

problem: An animal shelter had 27 puppies ready for new homes. On Saturday, 9 of them were adopted. How many puppies were still at the shelter?
follow_up_questions: On Sunday, 6 more puppies were adopted. How many were left then?
The shelter puts the remaining puppies into pens of 4. How many pens does it need?
Each adoption over the weekend cost a $5 fee. How much did the shelter collect in fees?

problem: On Saturday a bike shop sold 9 of its 27 used bikes. How many used bikes were left in the shop?
follow_up_questions: On Sunday it sold 6 more. How many used bikes were left after that?
The shop lines up the leftover bikes in racks that hold 4 each. How many racks does it fill?
For every bike sold over the weekend, the shop charged a $5 delivery fee. How much did it get in delivery fees?

problem: Ignacio sold his old video games at a yard sale and made $80. He spent $35 of it on a new controller. How much money does he still have?
follow_up_questions: He adds the $15 he got for mowing a lawn. How much does he have now?
He divides it equally among 3 envelopes. How much goes in each envelope?

problem: How much money is left for Ayumi? Her bake sale table brought in $80, and $35 of that went on new baking trays.
follow_up_questions: Her aunt gives her $15 for her birthday. How much money does Ayumi have now?
She shares it equally between 3 piggy banks. How much goes into each one?

problem: When the lemonade stand opened, Gustavo's tin held $26. By lunch it held $71. How much did he take in during the morning?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon he takes in $18 more. How much is in the tin when he closes?

problem: How much money did the ticket booth at the school fair take in before noon? The booth started the day with $26 in its drawer, and at noon the drawer held $71.
follow_up_questions: After noon the booth took in another $18. How much was in the drawer when the fair ended?

problem: Each flashlight in the camping shop needs 4 batteries. A scout leader buys 6 flashlights for the troop. How many batteries do the flashlights need?
How many wheels are there on 6 toy trucks if every truck has 4 wheels? Liang lines the trucks up on his bedroom floor to count.
Paintbrushes at the art shop come in sets of 6. Ms. Kowalski needs 42 brushes for her art students. How many sets should she buy?
follow_up_questions: Each set costs $8. How much will she spend?
The school gave her $70 for brushes. How much of it will be left over?

problem: How many boxes of light bulbs must the caretaker buy? He needs 42 bulbs for the gym, and bulbs are sold in boxes of 6.
follow_up_questions: A box costs $8. What will the bulbs cost him?
He has a $70 budget for bulbs. How much money will he have left?

problem: Olumide has $47 to spend at the garden centre. Each potted plant costs $9. What is the largest number of plants he can buy?
follow_up_questions: How much money will he have left after buying them?

problem: Saskia's class has $47 for a trip to the cinema, and every ticket costs $9. How many tickets can the class buy at most?
follow_up_questions: How much money will be left once those tickets are bought?

problem: At the bookshop, a cookbook costs $17. Mateus pays with three $10 bills. How much change does he get back?
follow_up_questions: He also buys a $5 bookmark out of his change. How much money does he have now?
His grandmother gives him enough to double that amount. How much does he have now?
How many $4 notebooks could he buy with that money?

problem: Three $10 bills go across the counter when Yuki buys a $17 lunch box at the department store. What change should she get?
follow_up_questions: With some of the change she buys a $5 water bottle. How much is left?
Her mum adds enough to double what she has. How much does she have now?
How many $4 pencil cases could she buy with it?

problem: Mikael bought 5 packs of trading cards, and each pack holds 8 cards. He keeps them in a shoebox under his bed. How many cards did he buy?
follow_up_questions: He trades 12 of the cards to a friend. How many does he keep?

problem: How many crayons did Ama get? Ama loves drawing horses. Her uncle bought her 5 tins of crayons with 8 crayons in each tin.
follow_up_questions: She gives 12 of the crayons to her little brother. How many does she keep?

problem: Each tray in the school canteen holds a dozen sandwiches. The cook fills 7 trays for sports day. How many sandwiches does she make?
follow_up_questions: She packs the sandwiches into lunch boxes of 6. How many boxes can she fill?
Each lunch box sells for $5. How much money does the canteen raise?

problem: How many eggs does a farmer collect if she fills 7 cartons that each hold a dozen eggs?
follow_up_questions: She repacks them into small boxes of 6 for the market. How many small boxes does she fill?
Each small box sells for $5. How much money does she make?

problem: Mrs. Bello took 45 leaflets about the town clean-up to hand out at the market. When she left, she still had 17. How many leaflets did she hand out?
follow_up_questions: The next day she handed out the same number again. How many did she hand out over the two days?
She had hoped to hand out 70 leaflets on those days. How many short of her goal is she?
She will make up the difference over 2 more days, handing out the same number each day. How many leaflets is that each day?

problem: How many stickers did Rafael give away? He brought 45 stickers to the school assembly and came home with 17.
follow_up_questions: On the following day he gave away exactly as many again. What is his total for the two days?
He wanted to give away 70 stickers on those days. How many short is he?
He plans to give away the shortfall evenly over 2 more days. How many stickers per day is that?

problem: Lena saved $85 for a camping trip. She spends $28 on a sleeping bag and $19 on a flashlight and batteries. How much of her savings is left?
follow_up_questions: The campsite fee is $15. After she pays it, how much money does Lena have?

problem: How much of Hamid's $85 is left after he buys football boots for $28 and shin pads for $19?
follow_up_questions: Then he pays the $15 club fee. How much money does Hamid have now?

problem: Kemal has saved $39 toward a guitar. The guitar costs $64. How much more money does he need?
follow_up_questions: He saves $5 every week. How many weeks will it take him to save the rest?
He also wants a guitar case for $12. What will the guitar and the case cost together?

problem: A $64 microscope is on Olga's wish list, and so far she has put away $39. How much is she still missing?
follow_up_questions: If she saves $5 each week, how many weeks will she need to save the rest?
She would also like a box of slides for $12. How much do the microscope and the slides cost together?

problem: Every week Haruto puts $6 of his allowance in a tin for new hiking boots. How much will he have saved after 9 weeks?
follow_up_questions: The hiking boots cost $72. How much more does he need?

problem: Leticia is saving for a tent. How much will be in her savings box after 9 weeks if she adds $6 to it each week?
follow_up_questions: The tent she wants costs $72. How much more must she save?

problem: At the craft club, each paper lantern takes 8 sheets of coloured paper. The club has 56 sheets. How many lanterns can they make?
How many bird feeders can the scouts fill from 56 scoops of seed, if each feeder takes 8 scoops?
In the school garden, the children planted 8 rows of sunflowers with 6 sunflowers in each row. Then rabbits ate 19 of the sunflowers. How many sunflowers are still standing?
follow_up_questions: The next week they plant 3 more rows of the same length. How many sunflowers are standing now?
Then a storm knocks down 21 sunflowers. How many are still standing?

problem: How many photos can still be seen on the class noticeboard? It was covered with 8 rows of photos, 6 photos to a row, before a big poster was pinned over 19 of them.
follow_up_questions: Later the class pins up 3 more rows of the same length. How many photos can be seen now?
Then a new timetable covers 21 more photos. How many can still be seen?

problem: The hardware store had 70 bags of potting soil. It sold 24 bags on Friday and 31 bags on Saturday. How many bags are left?
follow_up_questions: A delivery brings 40 more bags. How many bags does the store have now?
The bags are stacked in piles of 5. How many piles are there?

problem: How many boxes of paper are left in the school storeroom? It held 70 boxes, and then teachers took 24 in the first week of term and 31 in the second.
follow_up_questions: The office orders 40 more boxes. How many boxes are in the storeroom now?
The boxes go on shelves, 5 boxes to a shelf. How many shelves are filled?

problem: At the music shop, Ingrid sees a keyboard for sixty dollars and a guitar for forty-five dollars. What is the difference between their prices?
How much less does a raincoat cost than rain boots, if the boots are sixty dollars and the raincoat is forty-five dollars?
A wedding planner has 58 candles for the reception, and each table gets 6 candles. How many tables can have a full set of candles?
follow_up_questions: How many candles are left over?
The planner finds just enough extra candles to give one more table a full set. How many extra candles does she find?
How many tables have a full set of candles now?

problem: How many full boxes of 6 can a baker pack from 58 doughnuts?
follow_up_questions: How many doughnuts are left over?
She fries just enough extra doughnuts to fill one more box. How many extra doughnuts does she fry?
How many full boxes are there now?

problem: A florist ties 50 roses into bunches of 8. After she makes as many full bunches as she can, how many roses are left over?
follow_up_questions: Each full bunch sells for $3. How much money will the full bunches bring in?

problem: How many marbles are left over when Dov puts 50 marbles into bags of 8, filling as many bags as he can?
follow_up_questions: He sells each full bag for $3. How much will the full bags bring in?

problem: Ruth is saving for a $72 telescope. For every $5 she saves, her grandmother adds $3. How much of the price will Ruth pay herself?
follow_up_questions: How much will her grandmother put in?
Ruth earns her share by washing cars for $9 a car. How many cars must she wash?

problem: How much will Diego pay toward a $72 bike if his father adds $3 for every $5 Diego saves?
follow_up_questions: What will his father's share be?
Diego earns his part by raking leaves at $9 per garden. How many gardens must he rake?

problem: Each rowing boat at the lake holds 4 children. A class of 22 children wants to go out on the water at the same time. How many boats do they need so that everyone gets a seat?
How many taxis must be ordered for 22 wedding guests, if each taxi can carry 4 guests and nobody is to be left behind?
The bill for the team's end-of-season dinner was $96, and the 8 coaches shared it equally. How much did each coach pay?
follow_up_questions: One coach paid with a $20 bill. How much change did that coach get?

problem: How much does each of 8 friends pay if they split a $96 bowling bill equally?
follow_up_questions: One friend hands over a $20 bill. What change does that friend get?

problem: For sports day, the school needs 48 oranges. At the market, oranges are sold at 6 for $2. The oranges come from a farm by the river. What will the oranges cost?
follow_up_questions: The school pays with a $20 bill. What is the change?
Next year the school needs twice as many oranges. How much will those oranges cost?

problem: What does it cost Mr. Lindgren to buy 48 pencils, if the shop sells them at 6 for $2? He prefers pencils with erasers on the end.
follow_up_questions: He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get?
Next term he needs twice as many pencils. What will they cost?

problem: A pie at the bakery is $7, and a birthday cake costs $9 more than the pie. Find the cake's price.
follow_up_questions: Bongani buys one cake and one pie. How much does he spend?

problem: How much does a football cost at the sports shop? It is $9 more than a pair of socks, and the socks cost $7.
follow_up_questions: Elena buys one football and one pair of socks. What does she spend?

problem: A baker iced 24 cupcakes for a party. She used pink icing on 15 and chocolate icing on all the others. How many cupcakes got chocolate icing?
How many bikes in the school bike rack are blue? The rack holds 24 bikes; 15 are red, and every other one is blue.
Chen took $40 to the aquarium gift shop and spent $23 on a toy shark. How much money does he have left?
follow_up_questions: Then he buys a postcard for $4. How much does he have now?

problem: How much is left in Mariana's purse? She had $40 and paid $23 for sandals at the market.
follow_up_questions: She also buys a $4 hair clip. How much money is left now?

problem: To make one long garden hose, Mr. Popescu joined a 13-metre hose to a 9-metre hose. How long is the joined hose?
follow_up_questions: He cuts off 4 metres that had a leak. How long is the hose now?

problem: How long is the paper chain when Nia joins her 13-foot chain to her sister's 9-foot one?
follow_up_questions: They tear off 4 feet to decorate the door. How long is the chain now?

problem: There are 30 children at swimming camp. 12 of them swim in the deep pool and the rest are in the shallow pool. How many children are in the shallow pool?

Each child in the shallow pool needs a float that costs $2. How much do the floats for all of them cost?
The camp has $50 to spend. How much will be left after buying the floats?

problem: How many dancers are in the tap group? The dance school has 30 students: 12 take ballet and the others take tap.
follow_up_questions: The tap dancers stand in 3 equal rows. How many are in each row?
Each tap dancer needs a $2 ribbon for the show. What do the ribbons cost altogether?
The school has $50 for the show. How much will remain after the ribbons are bought?

problem: Alessandro opens his piggy bank and finds six $5 bills inside. How much money is that?
follow_up_questions: He spends $22 on a model airplane. How much money does he have left?

problem: How much money did Grandpa give Thandi, if her birthday card held six $5 bills?
follow_up_questions: She spends $22 on a new backpack. How much is left?

problem: A school canteen needs 72 bread rolls for the sports day lunch. Rolls are sold in bags of a dozen. How many bags must the cook buy?
follow_up_questions: Each bag costs $4. How much does the cook spend on rolls?
She pays with a $50 bill. What change does she get?

problem: How many boxes of a dozen pencils does a teacher need to buy to get 72 pencils?
follow_up_questions: The boxes are $4 each. How much does she spend?
She hands over a $50 bill. How much change comes back?

problem: At the zoo, Marek spent 25 minutes watching the penguins and 35 minutes at the monkey house. A peacock wandered across the path. How long did he spend at the zoo?
follow_up_questions: His sister stayed 15 minutes less than he did. How long did she stay?

problem: How many minutes did Saanvi practise? Her cat slept on the sofa the whole time. She played piano for 25 minutes and then violin for 35 minutes.
follow_up_questions: Her friend practised 15 minutes less than Saanvi. How long did her friend practise?

problem: Ananya carried 52 marbles in a paper bag. On the bus ride home, 17 rolled out through a tear. How many marbles were still in the bag when she got home?
How many apples reached the market? The farmer's cart held 52 apples, but 17 bounced off on the bumpy road.
For football practice, Jonas needs a $9 water bottle and $14 shin pads. How much money does he need for both?
What does Yasmin pay at the stationery shop for a $14 pencil case and a $9 ruler set?

follow_up_questions: She cuts the rest into pieces 8 centimetres long. How many pieces does she get?
Each piece becomes a hair bow that sells for $3. How much money can the bows bring in?

problem: How much fence wire is left after Farmer Aziz cuts 27 metres from a 75-metre roll to fix the goat pen?
follow_up_questions: He cuts the leftover wire into pieces 8 metres long. How many pieces does that give?
He sells each piece to a neighbour for $3. How much money can he get for them?

problem: A teacher has 33 new library books for her class. She has already covered 14 of them in plastic. How many books still need covering?
How many seedlings in the greenhouse still need watering, if there are 33 seedlings and the gardener has watered 14 so far?
The town's cycle path was 46 kilometres long. This year workers built 28 more kilometres. How long is the cycle path now?
follow_up_questions: Next year the town plans another 15 kilometres. How long will the path be then?

problem: How long is the hedge around the park now? It used to be 46 metres long, and this spring the gardeners planted another 28 metres.
follow_up_questions: Next spring they plan to plant 15 more metres. How long will the hedge be then?

problem: On the pond, 9 ducks and 4 swans are swimming. How many more ducks than swans are there?
follow_up_questions: Then 6 more swans land on the pond. How many swans are there now?
How many more swans than ducks are there now?
How many birds are on the pond in all?

problem: How many more adults than children are riding the bus? There are 9 adult passengers and 4 child passengers aboard.
follow_up_questions: At the next stop, 6 more children get on. How many children are on the bus now?
Now how many more children than adults are on the bus?
What is the total number of passengers on the bus now?

problem: A tent in the camping shop costs $58. Paulo has only $41. How much more money does he need?
follow_up_questions: His uncle gives him $25. After buying the tent, how much money will he have left over?
He spends the leftover on tent pegs that cost $4 a bag. How many bags can he buy?

problem: How much is Svetlana short if she has $41 and the ice skates she wants cost $58?
follow_up_questions: Her grandfather gives her $25. How much will she have left after buying the skates?
She spends what is left on laces at $4 a pair. How many pairs can she buy?

problem: On a nature walk, Amaya spotted 47 butterflies and Teodor spotted 39. What is the difference between their counts?
follow_up_questions: Teodor looks again and spots 11 more butterflies in the flowers. What is his new count?

problem: By how many votes did Ruby beat Kaito in the school election, if Ruby got 47 votes and Kaito got 39?
follow_up_questions: A recount finds 11 more votes for Kaito. What is his new total?

problem: A pottery class lasts 75 minutes. Grace has been working on her bowl for 48 minutes. The studio has big windows. How many minutes of class are left?
follow_up_questions: After class she waits 13 minutes for her mother to pick her up. How many minutes from now until her mother arrives?
The drive home takes 25 minutes. How many minutes from now until Grace gets home?

problem: How much longer is the film? The cinema seats are soft and blue. The film runs for 75 minutes, and Henrik has watched 48 minutes of it.
follow_up_questions: After the film ends he waits 13 minutes for the tram. How many minutes from now until the tram comes?
The tram ride home takes 25 minutes. How many minutes from now until Henrik is home?

problem: A bicycle at the sports store costs $85 and a scooter costs $49. How much less does the scooter cost?
follow_up_questions: The store takes $10 off the bicycle. What is the difference in price now?

problem: How much cheaper is a $49 tent than an $85 kayak at the outdoor shop?
follow_up_questions: The kayak goes on sale for $10 off. What is the difference between the two prices now?

problem: Felix is reading a 64-page comic book on the train. He has read 38 pages. How many pages are left?
How many pages of her 64-page sticker album has Wanjiru still not filled, if she has filled 38?
The school choir sold cookies and raised $93. It spent $56 of that on a bus to a singing contest. How much money does the choir still have?
follow_up_questions: A grandparent donates another $25. How much does the choir have now?

problem: How much is left of the $93 the football team raised at its car boot sale, after $56 is spent on new kits?
follow_up_questions: A local shop gives the team $25 more. How much does the team have now?

problem: There are 8 tables at the school bake sale. Each table puts out 3 trays of brownies. How many trays of brownies are there?
follow_up_questions: A tray of brownies sells for $4. If every tray sells, how much money do the tables make?
The tables pay the school $30 altogether for the hall. How much money do they keep?

problem: How many boxes of strawberries are on display, if each of the 8 farm trucks at the fair unloads 3 boxes?
follow_up_questions: Every box sells for $4. How much money is made if all the boxes sell?
The farmers pay the fair $30 in total for parking. How much money do they keep?

problem: At the fun fair, each ride costs $3. Oskar wants to go on 9 rides. What will they cost him?
How much does Lucia pay for 9 bags of popcorn when one bag is $3?
At the swimming lesson, the coach puts the children into 6 lanes with 7 children in each lane. How many children are swimming?
follow_up_questions: Each child paid $5 for the lesson. How much did the coach collect?

problem: How many horses are in the riding school's parade if they walk in 6 lines of 7 horses each?
follow_up_questions: Each horse's rider paid $5 to join the parade. How much was collected in all?

problem: Aunt Mirela made 32 bars of soap and packs 4 bars into each gift box for the church fair. How many boxes does she make?
follow_up_questions: Each box sells for $9. How much money does she raise?
Visitors add $18 in donations. What is her total now?
She splits the money equally among 3 charities. How much does each charity get?

problem: How many bundles of 4 candles can Torvald make from the 32 candles he poured in his workshop for the winter market?
follow_up_questions: He sells each bundle for $9. How much money does he raise?
Friends add $18 in donations. What is his total now?
He divides the money equally among 3 animal shelters. How much does each shelter get?

problem: A zoo keeper needs 90 fish to feed the penguins. Fish come in buckets of 15. How many buckets does she need?
follow_up_questions: Each bucket costs $4. What will all the buckets cost?
Her budget for fish is $30. How much of the budget will be left?

problem: How many packs of 15 balloons does a party planner need to get 90 balloons?
follow_up_questions: Each pack costs $4. What do all the packs cost?
She has $30 set aside for balloons. How much of that will be left?

problem: The cash box at the school cake stall held $45, all in five-dollar bills. How many bills were in the box?
follow_up_questions: Then 7 more five-dollar bills were put in. How many bills are in the box now?

problem: How many five-dollar bills make up the $45 that Tamar keeps in her desk drawer?
follow_up_questions: She adds 7 more five-dollar bills to the drawer. How many bills are there now?

problem: Akosua spent $14 at the toy shop on Saturday. On Sunday she went back and spent $27 more. How much did she spend over the weekend?
follow_up_questions: She started the weekend with $60. How much does she have left?
Her brother has $8 more than Akosua has left. How much does her brother have?

problem: How much did Rashid spend at the market in all, if he spent $14 on bread in the morning and $27 on fruit in the afternoon?
follow_up_questions: He had $60 when he left home. How much does he have left?
His cousin has $8 more than Rashid has left. How much does his cousin have?

problem: The garden centre has 26 plant pots on a shelf. 9 are plastic and the rest are clay. How many clay pots are there?
follow_up_questions: Each clay pot needs a $3 saucer. What do the saucers cost altogether?

problem: How many of the 26 children at the party wore costumes, if 9 came in ordinary clothes?
follow_up_questions: Each child in a costume got a $3 prize. What did the prizes cost in total?

problem: At the zoo, one tortoise weighs 43 kilograms and another weighs 28 kilograms. How much heavier is the bigger tortoise?
What is the difference in weight between a 28-pound sack of flour and a 43-pound sack of potatoes in the shop's storeroom?
At the craft shop, Sakura chooses 8 balls of wool for a scarf. Each ball costs $7. What does she pay?
follow_up_questions: She gives the cashier $60. How much change does she get?

problem: What is the total when Desmond buys 8 movie tickets that cost $7 apiece?
follow_up_questions: He pays with $60. What change does he get?

problem: A school jacket costs $80, and Nomvula's mother pays for it with $20 bills only. How many bills does she use?
follow_up_questions: If she paid with $10 bills instead, how many bills would she need?
How many more bills is that than before?

problem: How many $20 bills cover the $80 price of a train ticket to the city?
follow_up_questions: How many bills would it take if they were $10 bills instead?
How many more bills is that?

problem: A sports club rents out its football pitch for $24 a game. Four teams each rent the pitch for one game. How much does the club collect?
follow_up_questions: Each team also pays $8 to use the changing rooms. How much do the changing rooms bring in?
What does the club collect from the pitch and the changing rooms together?

problem: How much does the craft market earn when 4 sellers each rent a table for $24?
follow_up_questions: Every seller also pays $8 for a sun umbrella. How much do the umbrellas bring in?
How much does the market collect from tables and umbrellas together?

problem: Three friends sold old toys at a yard sale and made $36. They split the money equally. How much does each friend get?
follow_up_questions: One friend spends $5 on a comic. How much does that friend have left?
Another friend doubles his share by mowing lawns. How much does he have now?
How much more does he have than the friend who bought the comic?

problem: How much does each sister get when 3 sisters share the $36 they earned picking berries?
follow_up_questions: One sister spends $5 on a hair band. How much does she have left?
Another sister doubles her share by babysitting. How much does she have now?
How much more does she have than the sister who bought the hair band?

problem: A swimming lesson costs $9. Kofi takes 8 lessons this summer. What does he pay?
follow_up_questions: He pays with $80. How much change does he get?
His cousin takes half as many lessons. How many lessons does his cousin take?

problem: What does Ylva pay for 8 riding lessons if each lesson is $9?
follow_up_questions: She hands over $80. What change does she get?
Her brother signs up for half as many lessons. How many lessons does he take?

problem: At the end of the school picnic, 4 classmates shared a big bag of 36 grapes so that everyone got the same number. How many grapes did each classmate get?
follow_up_questions: Each classmate ate 7 grapes and saved the rest. How many grapes were saved altogether?
Later the saved grapes were split between 2 teachers. How many did each teacher get?

problem: How many stickers did each of the 4 friends get from a sheet of 36 stickers that they shared out evenly at a sleepover?
follow_up_questions: Each friend used 7 stickers on a notebook and saved the rest. How many stickers were saved altogether?
The next morning, the saved stickers were split between 2 little sisters. How many did each sister get?

problem: At art club the children worked in 7 groups, and each group made 4 clay pots. How many clay pots were made?
follow_up_questions: Next week, every group plans to make 3 more pots than it did this week. How many pots will the club make then?
Over the two weeks, how many pots will the club have made altogether?

problem: How many paper boats were floated on the pond if 7 families each folded 4 boats at the Sunday picnic?
follow_up_questions: Next Sunday each family plans to fold 3 more boats than this time. How many boats will be floated then?
Over the two Sundays, how many boats will have been floated in total?

problem: A bus ride to the beach costs 4 dollars per person. On Saturday, 63 people took the bus. How much money did the bus company collect?
How much money did the school make from its puppet show, if it sold 63 tickets at 4 dollars each?
Mei carried home a 5-kilogram sack of rice from the market, and her uncle carried a sack 4 times as heavy. The market is 7 blocks from their house. How heavy was her uncle's sack, in kilograms?
follow_up_questions: They put both sacks on the scale together. How many kilograms did the scale show?

problem: How heavy is the big pumpkin, in kilograms? At the harvest fair, Laszlo, who is 7 years old, entered a pumpkin of 5 kilograms, and his grandmother entered one 4 times as heavy.
follow_up_questions: They put both pumpkins on one scale. How many kilograms does the scale show?

problem: On sports day the toy car race began. The small red car rolled down the ramp in 9 seconds, and the big wooden car took 4 times as long. How many seconds did the wooden car take?
follow_up_questions: By how many seconds did the red car beat the wooden one?
After its wheels were oiled, the wooden car became 12 seconds faster. What is its new time?

problem: How long did Ingrid's kite take to reach the treetops, in seconds? Benno's kite got there in 9 seconds, and Ingrid's needed 4 times as long.
follow_up_questions: How many seconds faster was Benno's kite?
With a longer tail, Ingrid's kite got there 12 seconds quicker the next day. What was its new time?

problem: For the school sports day, the coach needs 72 juice boxes, and juice boxes come in packs of 8. The coach has a loud silver whistle. How many packs must he buy?
follow_up_questions: The night before, he finds that 3 packs have leaked. How many good juice boxes does he have now?

problem: Work out how many packs of 8 paper plates a caterer must buy to have 72 plates for a garden party. The garden is full of roses.
follow_up_questions: She drops 3 packs in a puddle on the way, and those plates are ruined. How many usable plates does she have?

problem: After a weekend of selling cupcakes, 6 students had earned 54 dollars for their class trip. They shared it equally. How many dollars did each student get?
How many dollars does each of six band members get when they split the 54 dollars they earned playing at a street fair equally?
A gardener has a 58-metre roll of hose and cuts it into 9-metre pieces for the vegetable beds. After cutting as many pieces as she can, how much hose is left on the roll?
follow_up_questions: How many full pieces did she cut?

problem: How much string is left over when Kaveh cuts as many 9-centimetre pieces as he can from a 58-centimetre string for his kite tails?
follow_up_questions: How many full pieces did he get?

problem: Painting one birdhouse takes Ade 6 minutes, and the craft fair starts in 40 minutes. What is the largest number of birdhouses he can finish painting by then?
How many full laps can Signe run before her bus comes in 40 minutes, if one lap of the track takes her 6 minutes?
After the school fair, the teachers found 29 spare balloons. Mr. Petrov ties them into bunches of 8 for the classrooms. How many full bunches can he make?
follow_up_questions: How many balloons are left over without a full bunch?
The next day a pupil brings in 3 more balloons, which are added to the leftover ones. How many balloons are in that pile now?

problem: How many full packs of 8 can Rosalind make from the 29 seed packets left at the end of the garden club's sale?
follow_up_questions: How many seed packets are left over after that?
A week later a member drops off 3 more packets and adds them to the leftovers. How many leftover packets are there now?

problem: At the art workshop, the leader poured out 63 beads, and each child at the table took 7. How many children were at the table?
follow_up_questions: After a break, 4 of those children went to the painting corner and took their beads with them. How many beads stayed at the table?
Then the leader poured out 15 more beads. How many beads are at the table now?

problem: How many children were on the beach blanket if a parent shared out 63 shells and every child got 7?
follow_up_questions: Later, 4 of those children ran off to swim, taking their shells with them. How many shells were left on the blanket?
Then the parent added 15 more shells. How many shells are on the blanket now?

problem: For the school prize-giving, the caretaker set up 46 chairs in one long row at the front for the winners, plus 7 rows of 18 chairs behind them for the families. How many chairs did he set up?
follow_up_questions: When the prize-giving began, 9 chairs were empty. How many people were sitting down?
Each seated person got 2 programmes. How many programmes were handed out?

problem: How many seats are there in the circus tent? Behind a front row of 46 seats there are 7 rows with 18 seats each.
follow_up_questions: At the first show, 9 seats were empty. How many people sat down to watch?
Every person watching was given 2 balloons. How many balloons were given out?

problem: There were 23 children in the swimming pool. When the lifeguard blew his whistle for lunch, 9 of them climbed out. How many children stayed in the pool?
follow_up_questions: After lunch, 10 more children jumped into the pool. How many children were in the pool then?
They split up equally among the 4 lanes. How many children were in each lane?
Then 2 children from every lane got out to dry off. How many children were still in the lanes?

problem: How many children kept dancing? At the party, 23 children were on the dance floor until 9 of them left to eat cake.
follow_up_questions: After the cake, 10 more children came to dance. How many children were dancing then?
The party leader split them equally into 4 circles. How many children were in each circle?
Then 2 children from every circle sat down to rest. How many children were still in the circles?

problem: Before the school fair opened, 34 cookies were on the bake sale table. Then a parent brought another 18. How many cookies were ready to sell?
follow_up_questions: By noon, 28 cookies had been sold. How many were left?
The leftover cookies were packed into bags of 4. How many bags were filled?
Each bag sells for 7 dollars. How much money will the table make if every bag is sold?

problem: How many bread rolls were on the bakery shelf after the baker added 18 fresh ones to the 34 already there?
follow_up_questions: During the morning, 28 rolls were sold. How many were left?
In the afternoon, the leftover rolls were put into bags of 4. How many bags were filled?
A bag sells for 7 dollars. How much will the bakery take if every bag is sold?

problem: Mr. Novak painted 30 cardboard shields for the class pageant. The pageant tells the story of a brave knight. At the last practice, 13 shields got bent. How many shields are still good to use?
follow_up_questions: The next day he paints 8 new shields. How many good shields does he have now?
The class needs 28 shields in all. How many more must he paint before the show?

problem: How many masks are still usable for the dance show? Aunt Delia sewed 30 masks, but 13 were ripped at the dress rehearsal. The show takes place in the town hall.
follow_up_questions: She sews 8 new masks the next morning. How many usable masks are there now?
The dancers need 28 masks altogether. How many more must she sew?

problem: For the class party, Ms. Ferreira bought cakes that were each cut into 8 pieces. There were 56 pieces altogether. Work out how many cakes she bought.
follow_up_questions: The 14 pupils each ate 3 pieces. How many pieces were left for the teachers and parents?

problem: How many sandwich trays did the swimming coach order, if every tray held 8 sandwiches and there were 56 sandwiches in all?
follow_up_questions: The 14 swimmers each ate 3 sandwiches. How many sandwiches were left for the parents?

problem: Ines put 15 flower pots outside her plant stall on Sunday. Her neighbour was starting a stall too, so Ines gave her 8 of the pots. How many pots did Ines keep?
How many pencils does Rory have left after handing 8 of his 15 pencils to a classmate who forgot hers?
There were 31 swimmers at the lake on Saturday morning. Some went home at lunchtime, and after that only 17 remained. How many swimmers went home?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon, 25 swimmers came back. How many swimmers were at the lake then?

problem: How many shoppers left the market at noon, if thirty-one shoppers were there in the morning and just 17 were still there afterwards?
follow_up_questions: Later, 25 shoppers came in. How many shoppers were at the market then?

problem: Thirty-four children were in the opening scene of the school play. Between scenes, 12 of them went to change costumes and 5 others went to help with the lights. How many children stayed on stage?
follow_up_questions: After changing, the 12 children came back on stage for the next scene. How many children were on stage then?

problem: How many dancers were still on the floor? The dance show began with 34 dancers; at the break 12 left to put on new shoes, and 5 more went to get water.
follow_up_questions: When the 12 dancers came back in their new shoes, how many dancers were on the floor?

problem: On Friday the bakery sold 4 white loaves for every brown loaf. If it sold 36 white loaves, how many brown loaves did it sell?
follow_up_questions: How many loaves of the two kinds were sold in all?
Saturday was twice as busy for those loaves. How many were sold on Saturday?

problem: How many red tulips are in the park's flower bed? The gardener planted 4 yellow tulips for every red one, and there are 36 yellow tulips.
follow_up_questions: How many tulips of those two colours are in the bed altogether?
A second bed has twice as many of those tulips. How many tulips are in the second bed?

problem: The garden club meets every 2 weeks. In Teo's garden there are 6 tomato plants for every pepper plant, and he has 7 pepper plants. How many tomato plants does he have?
follow_up_questions: His friend Ilse has 9 fewer tomato plants than Teo. How many does Ilse have?

problem: How many green beads are on Kalinda's necklace? She has threaded 6 green beads for every white bead, and there are 7 white beads. The necklace took her 2 afternoons to make.
follow_up_questions: Her sister's necklace has 9 fewer green beads than Kalinda's. How many green beads are on her sister's necklace?

problem: Odile sorted the buttons in her grandmother's tin on a snowy afternoon. There were 8 red buttons, and she counted 4 blue buttons for each red one. What was the total number of red and blue buttons?
How many cows and sheep are in the field altogether, if there are 8 cows and 4 sheep for every cow?
Over three days, the school band sold cupcakes at its bake sale for 5 dollars each: 19 on Sunday, 26 on Saturday and 14 on Friday. What was the total number of cupcakes sold?
follow_up_questions: Each cupcake cost 5 dollars. How much money did the band make?

problem: How many kites did the toy shop sell in its spring sale? Kites were priced at 5 dollars, and the shop sold 14 in the first hour, 26 later that morning and 19 in the afternoon.
follow_up_questions: Every kite sold for 5 dollars. How much money did the shop take in?

problem: Some ducks were swimming on the pond. Then 14 more flew down, and now there are 41 ducks on the pond. How many ducks were there at first?
follow_up_questions: Later, 18 of the ducks flew away. How many ducks are still on the pond?

problem: How many people were in the library before the rain started? When it began to pour, 14 people came in for shelter, which brought the total to 41.
follow_up_questions: Once the rain stopped, 18 of them left. How many people were still in the library?

problem: Marisol read 15 books this summer, which is 9 fewer than her cousin Arjun read. How many books did Arjun read?
follow_up_questions: How many books did the two of them read together?
Next summer Arjun wants to read 30 books. How many more is that than this summer?

problem: How many goals did Bruno score this season, if Kenta's 15 goals were 9 fewer than Bruno's?
follow_up_questions: What is the total number of goals the two boys scored?
Bruno's target for next season is 30 goals. How many more goals is that than this season?

problem: A farmer will share 96 bales of hay equally among the 4 barns on her farm. Her dog likes to sleep on the hay. How many bales will each barn get?
How many chairs go into each corner of the hall, if the caretaker spreads 96 chairs equally among its 4 corners? The hall floor was polished yesterday.
Amani has borrowed 16 library books this term. That is twice as many as her friend Sven has borrowed. How many books has Sven borrowed?
follow_up_questions: Each book borrowed earns 5 reading points. How many points has Sven earned?
Sven needs 60 points for a prize. How many more points does he need?

problem: How many stamps are in Ravi's album, if Cleo's album has 16 stamps and that is double the number in Ravi's?
follow_up_questions: Each stamp is worth 5 points in the club game. How many points does Ravi have?
Ravi needs 60 points to win a badge. How many more points does he need?

problem: Grandma Nell bought 40 apples on Monday to bake pies for the church sale. When she finished baking on Friday, 6 apples were left. How many apples did she use?
follow_up_questions: Every pie took 2 apples. How many pies did she bake?

problem: How many oranges did the juice stall use? It started the day with 40 oranges and had 6 left at closing.
follow_up_questions: Each glass of juice took 2 oranges. How many glasses did the stall make?

problem: Before the piano recital, Ines still has 23 bars of music to memorise and Callum has 16. How many more bars does Ines have to memorise than Callum?
follow_up_questions: Her teacher then shortens her piece by 5 bars. How many bars does she have to memorise now?
Now how many more bars than Callum does she have to memorise?

problem: How many more pages does Zuri have left to read than Mattias? Zuri has 23 pages to go in her library book, while Mattias has 16 pages to go in his.
follow_up_questions: That evening Zuri reads 5 pages. How many pages does she have left now?
How many more pages than Mattias does she have left now?

problem: At the end of the party there were 9 sandwiches left. The host cut each one in half to give out as snacks the next morning. How many snack pieces did she have?
follow_up_questions: By lunchtime the next day, 11 pieces had been eaten. How many were still on the plate?

problem: How many apple halves does the zoo keeper have after slicing 9 apples in half for the monkeys?
follow_up_questions: The monkeys gobble up 11 of the halves. How many halves are left?

problem: After the coin club met on Thursday, Lior gave 37 of his old coins to new members. He still has 68 coins. How many coins did Lior have before the meeting?
follow_up_questions: On Friday he swapped 8 of his coins for a magnifying glass. How many coins does he have now?
He sorts them into 6 equal stacks. How many coins are in each stack?
Then he adds 3 new coins to every stack. How many coins does he have in all now?

problem: How many shells did Moana start with, if she gave 37 shells to her friends at the beach and still has 68?
follow_up_questions: Later she trades 8 shells for a bracelet. How many shells does she have now?
She arranges them in 6 equal rows on her shelf. How many shells are in each row?
Then she puts 3 new shells at the end of every row. How many shells does she have in all now?

problem: The swimming coach wants one medal for each of the 27 swimmers at the gala. Medals come in boxes of 8. How many boxes does he need to buy?
follow_up_questions: After every swimmer has one medal, how many medals will be spare?

problem: How many packs of 8 party hats must Elif buy so that each of the 27 guests at her grandmother's birthday gets a hat?
follow_up_questions: Once every guest has a hat, how many hats will be left over?

problem: For the science fair, the teacher puts out 3 lamps for every 12 desks. There are 48 desks in the hall. How many lamps does she need?
follow_up_questions: On the morning of the fair, she finds that 5 of the lamps are broken. How many working lamps does she have?
The library lends her 9 lamps. How many lamps can she use now?

problem: How many water jugs does the caterer need for 48 guests if she puts out 3 jugs for every 12 guests?
follow_up_questions: Before the meal, 5 jugs crack. How many good jugs are left?
A neighbour brings over 9 jugs. How many jugs can the caterer use now?

problem: In the school mosaic, there are 2 gold tiles for every 7 white tiles. If the mosaic has 35 white tiles, how many gold tiles does it have?

follow_up_questions: Next month the session will run 2 hours longer. What will that one cost?
How much more will the longer session cost than this one?

problem: What will the Harrisons pay a clown for a 4-hour birthday party, if the clown charges 25 dollars per hour and 15 dollars extra for travel?
follow_up_questions: For the next party they want the clown for 2 more hours. What will that party cost?
How much more is the longer party than the first one?

problem: On Saturday, Ahmed folded 13 paper cranes at the craft club. His favourite colour is orange. On Sunday he folded 8 more at home. How many cranes has he folded so far?
How many laps has Solveig swum this week? The pool water was very cold. She swam 13 laps on Monday and 8 more on Wednesday.
The classroom wall already had 64 drawings pinned to it. Before parents' evening, Ms. Kaur pinned up 7 more. How many drawings are on the wall now?
follow_up_questions: Each drawing was held up by 2 pins. How many pins were used for all of them?

problem: How many badges are on the scout banner now? It had 64 badges sewn on, and at Friday's camp the scouts added 7 more.
follow_up_questions: Each badge cost 2 dollars. How much did all the badges on the banner cost?

problem: The children stacked 52 wooden blocks into a tower at nursery. In the afternoon, 17 blocks were knocked off. How many blocks were left in the tower?
follow_up_questions: Then they added 9 new blocks. How many blocks are in the tower now?

problem: How many sandbags were still on the river bank after 17 of the 52 sandbags were washed away by the flood?
follow_up_questions: Volunteers carried down 9 new sandbags. How many sandbags are on the bank now?
The bank needs 50 sandbags to be safe. How many more must the volunteers bring?

problem: Before the cafe opened, Matteo peeled 28 oranges. At lunchtime he peeled another 30. What is the total number of oranges he peeled?
follow_up_questions: Each glass of juice needs 2 oranges. How many glasses can he make?

He poured the leftover juice into jugs that hold 4 glasses each. How many jugs did he fill?

problem: How many carrots did the farm kitchen scrub? In the morning it scrubbed 28, and in the afternoon it scrubbed 30 more.
follow_up_questions: Each bowl of soup needs 2 carrots. How many bowls can the kitchen make?
